text: You already met onLoad, onChange, and onSubmit as form event hooks back in JavaScript for ServiceNow Developers. This lesson pushes all three to developer depth and adds a real fourth type, onCellEdit, which fires in a list view instead of a form entirely.

onChange's real signature is control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading, isTemplate. The control parameter is legacy — never use it to read or set values, that's g_form's job. oldValue and newValue always arrive as strings, even for a numeric or reference field, so compare with double equals, not strict equals. And always guard the top of the function against isLoading and isTemplate, or your logic will fire once when the form simply loads.

onSubmit takes no parameters, and the platform only blocks a save when the function returns the literal value false. Displaying an error message with g_form.addErrorMessage does nothing on its own — if you forget that explicit return false line, the record saves anyway, even though the user saw an error on screen.

onCellEdit's real signature is sysIDs, table, oldValues, newValue, callback. It fires when a user inline-edits a cell directly in a list, with no form involved — sysIDs and oldValues can describe multiple records at once, because a list lets someone select several rows and edit a shared cell in one action. The edit stays pending until your script calls callback of true to allow it or callback of false to block and revert it. And because there's no form here, there's no g_form — use g_list for messages instead.

So four types split across two contexts: onLoad, onChange, and onSubmit all run on a form with g_form available. onCellEdit runs on a list, has no g_form, and resolves through callback rather than a return value.
Next, Lesson 8 covers client script best practices in real depth — keeping these scripts fast and lightweight, and why client-side GlideRecord is no longer the right tool for reaching server data.
